RT by @hey_itsmyturn: Four Iranian airmen flew toward Qatar. One returned in a coffin. Three disappeared. 🇮🇷🇶🇦 For nearly five months, Iran officially called them missing. Now Tehran says Qatar has been hiding them alive since March. That sudden transformation is the real story. The two Su-24 bombers were shot down near Qatar on March 2. There is no evidence that either aircraft force-landed. No runway emergency, intact airframe or crash site on land was reported. If the three men survived, they almost certainly ejected over the Gulf. That is not impossible. The Su-24’s K-36D escape seats were designed to function even at extremely low altitude. But the aircraft were reportedly flying around 80 feet above the sea when engaged. Survival would have depended on the missile impact, aircraft attitude, parachute deployment and how quickly rescuers reached them. Qatar controlled the airspace, radar picture and surrounding waters. If the pilots entered the sea alive, Qatari forces were probably the first people capable of finding them. So Iran’s accusation is physically plausible. But Tehran has shown nothing to prove it. No photographs. No emergency-beacon data. No intercepted communications. No rescue coordinates. No witnesses. No message from the pilots. No ICRC confirmation. On July 29, Iran’s Army still said their fate was unknown. Two weeks later, Gen Mohammad Bagherzadeh claimed Qatar had held all three for six months. Either Iran recently obtained extraordinary intelligence and is refusing to reveal it, or the fate of three missing airmen is being rewritten into a politically useful hostage story. The TIMING matters. Qatar is currently carrying messages between Tehran and Washington. Accusing Doha of concealing Iranian prisoners gives Tehran leverage over the mediator and turns a disastrous, disputed air mission into a national grievance. Qatar also benefits from denial. Acknowledging prisoners would expose details of the interception, trigger ICRC access and prisoner-of-war obligations, risk Iranian retaliation and damage Doha’s attempt to appear neutral while hosting Al Udeid. But Qatar is also asking the world to trust information it has not released. It controls the radar recordings, engagement data and search-and-rescue logs. None has been made public. Doha says it invited Iranian investigators in April and received no response. Tehran says its team has spent months waiting for Qatar to let it enter. Someone is not telling the whole story.👀 The pilots may have died at sea. They may have been rescued and detained. Iran may be manufacturing certainty where none exists. Qatar may be concealing what its forces recovered. For now, three men remain trapped between two governments, two sealed military archives and two stories that cannot both be true.
It’s only going to get bigger, too.
